## Summary

Hardens disaster-recovery capture and Employment Decision Governance, adds authority-of-record qualification, and rehearses the Production migration chain against the verified 12 October backup. The rehearsal exposed service-role approval updates that could omit an actor or self-approve. A new forward migration and session-bound server action require an audited transition and reject self-approval.

Draft; no merge or deployment. Production and live account dispositions are unchanged. Automatic Vercel deployment is disabled for this PR branch.

## Current qualification

- Verified original custom archive: 4,103,536 bytes; SHA-256 `081310d3c1f64aaacf3c2207efa62bfa7641c81a670d5e23de6d11ae64784307`. Original archive and manifest preserved.
- Fresh isolated PostgreSQL restore and all 15 migrations passed. Ledger 119â†’134; all 11,133 original rows across 284 tables preserved. Exactly five PENDING approval rows and five request events were backfilled.
- Restored native database: 35 approval/V1/RLS/Trust Gateway checks, 25 authority/HTTP/MCP/receipt/Replay/Trust Memory checks, and five guarded failure/retry controls passed. Synthetic administrators and provider sessions only; no hosted-browser or external-provider result is inferred.
- Full local suite: 2,048 passed, zero failed/skipped. Final core-closure suite including the new approval regression: 22 passed. Security-closure: 16 passed. Typecheck passed; lint passed with 18 pre-existing warnings; redacted Gitleaks scan of staged files passed. Local production build passed. On `d6fa4f4`, CodeQL/analyze, Gitleaks, [CI verify](https://github.com/emeaexecutive/Cyber-Sentinels-V2/actions/runs/38229517849/job/114745250101) and [secret-free Docker qualification](https://github.com/emeaexecutive/Cyber-Sentinels-V2/actions/runs/38229517849/job/114745250166) all passed. Supabase Preview was skipped and is not counted as a pass. Vercel and GitHub deployment queries returned zero deployments for this push.
- Staging's current effective application schema matches the original 14-migration result. The new fix produces five expected differences requiring Staging application and qualification. Six local-only and 21 Staging-only versions (seven same-name pairs) are inventoried; no history was rewritten.
- One Storage object was separately captured and verified. This does not prove synchronized DB/Storage recovery. Native libpq verified-TLS controls cover the laptop-to-pooler hop; the reported backend `ssl = f` is not a whole-chain TLS pass.

## Review evidence

- [Rehearsal, exact reviewed migration commands, failure handling and approval gates](docs/operations/PRODUCTION-MIGRATION-REHEARSAL-20261012.md)
- [Qualification evidence with dated superseding addendum](docs/governance/PR-116-QUALIFICATION-EVIDENCE.md)
- [Backup, restore, TLS and separate Storage verification](docs/operations/PRODUCTION-BACKUP-VERIFICATION-20261012.md)
- [Source/execution hashes and row-preservation results](docs/operations/migration-rehearsal-20261012.json)
- [Staging ledger reconciliation](docs/operations/migration-ledger-reconciliation-20261012.json)

The prior hosted Staging employment/authority migrations and Preview checks remain historical evidence for their tested commit, not qualification of this new approval RPC. Spanish governance traceability remains in `docs/governance/SPANISH-EMPLOYMENT-DECISION-GOVERNANCE.md`; no legal-compliance claim is made.

## Remaining gates â€” Production NO-GO

1. Keith reviews the private redacted five-account inventory, selects two distinct authorized administrators and decides every live account disposition. No live account has been approved, rejected or suspended during rehearsal.
2. Qualify the new migration, server action and administrator bootstrap on Staging. Preserve historical ledger rows; any separate history repair needs source provenance and approval.
3. Approve a current recovery point, operator/change window and coordinated application/account transition. Applying approval enforcement makes all five existing accounts PENDING and denies their V1 keys until audited approval. The old admin page cannot write after the new privilege revocation.
4. Explicit owner approval is required before merge, deployment or Production migration execution. Offsite retention/recovery ownership, synchronized Storage requirements and legal/DPO decisions remain separate release decisions.

The reviewed generated Production SQL exactly matches the successful guarded rehearsal and rejects ledger drift. It has not been executed against Production. No automatic reverse migration or destructive restore is authorized.

In-flight HTTP and HTTP-carried MCP aborts are explicitly CANCELLATION_UNCONFIRMED, not proof that a remote side effect was reversed. Third-party cancellation remains unsupported. ## Summary
- Add a workload OIDC token verifier pinned to server-configured issuer, audience, and HTTPS JWKS; require validated signature, expiry, tenant, workload, subject, JTI, and the sole `trust:request` scope.
- Add owner/admin registration, listing, and revocation for tenant-owned workload bindings, plus a workload-only decision route that derives agent identity from the token and delegates to the existing canonical decision path.
- Add a service-role-only workload-binding migration, OpenAPI/SDK/PowerShell documentation, and focused security/contract tests.

## Security boundaries and limitations
- Workload credentials can request decisions only; this PR does not dispatch provider actions. ALLOW is not execution proof. HubSpot enforcement and uncertain-outcome reconciliation remain PR B.
- JWTs are bearer credentials during their short lifetime; no persistent JTI replay store is included. Bindings are revocable and decision requests require idempotency keys.
- The migration is not applied and no hosted issuer/database test has been performed. Hosted qualification remains blocked on approved non-production issuer/JWKS/audience configuration and database-backed cross-tenant/revocation tests.
- This PR uses the existing public API key authentication and current tenant owner/admin checks; it does not add the feature branch's separate account-approval schema.

## Validation
- Public API regression suite plus workload identity: 152 tests passed; the focused workload identity/schema suite: 7 passed.
- `npm run typecheck`, targeted ESLint, PowerShell parser, and `npm run build` passed.
- `npm audit --omit=dev`: zero production dependency advisories. `npm ci` reported 14 moderate findings in the full dependency set; none were auto-fixed.

No production deployment, schema application, provider credentials, or customer data are included.

An immutable table is unique by tenant/canonical transaction, request and approval; only the winning committed insertion grants dispatch. Approval scope snapshots bind executor, agent, action/destination/environment, parameter digest, authority/delegation and policy versions. Legacy unscoped approvals fail closed. Scope substitutions, invalid/reused approvals, expiry and revocation produce zero additional effects. Lost provider/claim responses and a disconnected application after claim preserve UNKNOWN and cannot redispatch. A rollback before commit leaves the approval usable. The test predecessor schema is minimal: this does not replace a full Staging migration rehearsal or real provider qualification. A dedicated exact-head CI workflow runs the same SQL tests using an ephemeral PostgreSQL service.

Availability tradeoff: a crash between claim and dispatch can leave zero effects and UNKNOWN. No automatic lease/reclaim is provided. Independent reconciliation must determine destination outcome; generic exactly-once remote execution is not claimed.

## Execution 03 â€” shared retry budget at the authority boundary

**Scope:** incremental change stacked on draft PR #139; retains PR #138 and #135 ancestry. This is NOT a Production release.

### Implemented
- Treat a trusted `quotaScope` with `quotaMode=AGGREGATE` as a shared retry/action allowance across descendant agents, operations, tools and resources. Keep the existing CAS-backed admission/append-only receipts and destination fence.
- Fail closed for invalid scoped quotas and for attempts to widen a previously established scoped limit within the same active window.
- Add regressions for competing agents racing for the final slot (one allowed effect and one denied attempt), delegated tool/operation switching, attempted limit expansion and invalid quota configuration.
- Include the new tests in the existing `test:swarm-authority` runner.

### Existing enforcement reused
- `createSwarmStore` per-tenant persistent CAS, current authority checks, budget reservations, emergency containment, Replay.
- No new table, remote API, external provider or independent authorization engine.

### Still not qualified
- Run and review exact-head GitHub CI; no local executable checkout was available in this connected-tool run.
- The scenario uses fixture-controlled destination effects, not hosted Postgres races or real provider delivery.
- Add **River Crossing: The Loop Limit** interactive UI after enforcement tests pass, and verify across a multi-connection Postgres/controlled destination. Scope enforcement must remain at the gateway; no arbitrary agent-supplied scope claims.
- No cancellation guarantee for work already dispatched. UNKNOWN requires reconciliation.
- Existing Staging migrations, full recovery, multi-tenant hosted and Production gates remain NO-GO.

**Do not merge, execute hosted migrations, perform hosted writes or deploy.**
